name: Suzanne Borstein
body:
Paul was one of my son, Andrew's, closest friends, from middle school onward. I saw him often during those years of growing up. Most often, I saw him at my back door, looking for Andrew. Sometimes, especially as they got older, I'd be getting ready for bed, and they'd be getting ready to go out and play pool.

Paul was easy to be with: friendly, open, helpful. When Andrew wasn't in town, Paul sometimes mowed my lawn and helped me with snow shoveling or yardwork. He was the first of Andrew's friends to call me by my first name, and I liked that. He had an easy familiarity. He was upbeat, open-hearted and generous.

He kept his beloved Porche in my garage, so I often saw him when he came by to work on it or take it out. He even treated me to a ride once, to share his pride and his joy.

Paul was a familiar face in the neighborhood. I often saw him riding his bike, and, after Oli was born, Paul wheeled him around Edgewood in his stroller. Once he pulled up next to me at a traffic light on Post Road, in one of his Volvos.  Another time he saw me in the parking lot at Ace Hardware and warned me that one of my tires had gone flat. He seemed to pop up so often, it's hard to accept that I won't see him again.

Oh, and did I mention that he made awesome hummis? My late husband's favorite.  We love you, Paul, and we miss you.

Suzanne/Susie Borstein
